principle: MATRIYA does not determine which evidence is needed to decide between hypotheses. It checks whether the evidence the scientist defined as discriminating actually exists.
note: The fourth primitive (Fresco). Knowledge / Evidence / Decision were three; Discriminability is the power of the EXISTING evidence to tell competing explanations apart — distinct from Evidence itself. A rich Evidence Set (viscosity+pH+density) has zero discriminability if H1 and H2 predict the same values for all of them. The check is LOGICAL, not scientific: are the human-declared discriminators present? It never infers WHAT discriminates.

boundary.system_does: check whether the human-declared discriminating observations are present in the evidence set
boundary.system_does_not: decide which evidence discriminates between hypotheses (that is the scientist's authorship)
boundary.on_missing_declaration: REFUSE — return status 'declaration_required'; do not infer a discriminator

hypothesis_declaration_contract.distinguished_by: array of observation/depth ids the SCIENTIST declares would distinguish this hypothesis from its competitors (human-authored, like the hypotheses themselves)

worked_example.statement: Cannot discriminate between H1 and H2 given current evidence.
worked_example.note: The Evidence Set is non-empty, yet none of the present observations is the declared discriminator. The fix is the declared discriminator (WP-001 recoverability), at the shallowest cost — not a re-run, not SEM/FTIR.
